h.title: HotLoop: industrial gateway, historian and alarms for PLCs
h.desc: Connect PLCs over OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, S7 and MQTT, keep the history, and raise ISA-18.2 alarms, on a Raspberry Pi or across every site.
h.ogAlt: HotLoop. Automation loops for the real world.
h.chip: Version {version} is out for all four core products
h.h1: Automation loops for the real world.
h.lede: HotLoop connects to your PLCs and devices, keeps the history, raises the alarms that matter, and moves a machine only when someone with the authority arms it. It runs on a Raspberry Pi next to one machine or across every site you operate, and it grows with you without a migration. Home and lab use is free, and businesses run it on EmberNet, starting with a free Pilot and moving to Starter or above for a production plant.
h.stat1: Native drivers for OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, Siemens S7, MQTT and Sparkplug B, CODESYS and more, each listed with exactly what it was tested against.
h.stat2: Flow node types that run your existing Node-RED flows, with every difference documented.
h.stat3: The whole Flow container image. It starts in a fraction of a second and runs on a Raspberry Pi 5. The full benchmark and method are on the Flow page.
h.prodText: Running in production at Shepherd Boy Farms, DayGlo and Trane Technologies through EmberNet.
h.loopH2: Sense, decide, act, and around again.
h.loopLede: HotLoop runs the loop so your people can walk away from it. It reports a dead sensor as a dead sensor, checks every rule when you save it, and refuses any write that is out of range or wasn't armed.
h.senseP: Reads real equipment over the protocols it already speaks and records the quality of every reading. A failed read is marked bad, so a dead sensor never trips every low alarm on the unit.
h.decideP: ISA-18.2 alarms, the industrial alarm standard, keep the trip that cleared on its own on the list for the next shift. Rules are checked the moment you save them.
h.actP: Every write, from an operator, a rule or an AI agent, passes through one gate with one set of checks, and every refusal is logged. See the write gate.
h.senseD: HotLoop polls real equipment over the protocols it already speaks and keeps the quality of every reading with the number. A failed read is marked bad, so a dead sensor doesn't trip every low alarm on the unit or send the night shift to check a tank that's fine.
h.decideD: ISA-18.2 alarms, the industrial alarm standard, including the alarm that cleared on its own before anybody saw it. It stays on the list for the next shift. Rules are checked when you save them, so a typo is caught in the editor before it reaches a batch.
h.actD: Every write, from an operator, a rule or an AI agent, passes through one gate. A value out of range is refused rather than quietly changed, and every refusal is logged. See the write gate in action.
h.prodsH2: Eight products, from a Pi on a shelf to the whole plant.
h.intH2: Every driver shows exactly what it was tested against.
h.intLede: Each integration lists the systems it has run against, so your team knows what day one looks like before commissioning starts. Protocols HotLoop doesn't speak natively come in through the gateway your site already has.
h.latestH2: What changed last, and whether you can download it.
h.licH2: Free to use. No license keys.
h.licLede: Every HotLoop product is under the HotLoop Source License Agreement 1.0. Home and lab use is free. Businesses run HotLoop on EmberNet, starting with a free Pilot for evaluation and pre-production, and Starter or above for a production plant, with no keys to enter and nothing locked behind a paywall. When you want a turnkey rollout with SLAs and a warranty, Fireball Industries, an authorized CODESYS distributor, technology partner and system integrator, designs and installs it, and EmberNet, HotLoop's Gold Licensee, supports it.
p.title: HotLoop products: compare IoT, Edge, Gateway, Flow and more
p.desc: Compare all eight HotLoop products for the plant floor, from a Raspberry Pi beside one machine to a gateway that runs the whole site.
p.ogAlt: The HotLoop lineup: IoT, Edge, Gateway, Edge Relay, Flow, Cascade, HotLoop for CODESYS, and Transmitter.
p.label: Products
p.lede: The first four share one codebase and one version, and every one of them speaks every protocol, MQTT included, so what you're really picking is how much of the plant the box has to run.
p.db.edge-relay: None. It holds readings until the uplink is back, and that is all
p.intro: What each product has, not whether it's finished. For that, open the product's page: every piece on it says whether it ships today or hasn't been built.
p.r5: MQTT discovery (Shelly, ESPHome, Tasmota, Zigbee2MQTT), read and forward only on the relay
p.r7: Historian targets in the plant's own database
p.r8: UniFi network driver, with commands off until armed (the screens and events need the UI)
p.r10: Dashboards, per role and per screen, with panel mode
p.r16: A web UI and a login
p.upP: Outgrowing the Pi should cost you an image pull, not a migration project. Every product runs the same data layout, so going from IoT to Edge to the Gateway is an image swap on the same database, with your devices, entities, rules, alarms, history, and users already there. Going back down deletes nothing: what the smaller product doesn't have just sits there until you come back. The move has been run on a plain Linux box, IoT to Edge to the Gateway on one database. On Kubernetes it is a chart upgrade, and a backup first is the habit that makes it boring.
p.keysP: No license keys, and nothing unlocks at runtime. The product is what got compiled, so a feature that isn't in your image can't be flipped on by accident, and nobody can flip one off to squeeze you later. All of HotLoop is free to use. Every product is under the HotLoop Source License Agreement 1.0, free for home and lab. What that means for you.
p.roadmaps: Where each one is headed: the HotLoop roadmap for the four core products, the Flow roadmap and the Cascade roadmap, the HotLoop for CODESYS roadmap, and the Transmitter roadmap. The docs for all eight are at docs.hotloop.io.
i.title: A loop, running
i.aria: A control loop cycling through sense, decide, and act
i.okNote: Inside deadband. No alarm raised, nothing paged.
i.warnNote: Outside the deadband, still under the on-delay. Not a page.
i.dangerNote: This is the one that wakes somebody at 03:00.
i.foot: A simulation in your browser. Drag the setpoint and watch the loop decide whether this is worth waking somebody up for. In the Gateway, the write that moves it crosses one gate. Out of range is refused and never clamped, and the refusal is written down.
